newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai exchange suspends Bangkok Bank of Commerce.
newsitem.headline: Thai exchange suspends Bangkok Bank of Commerce.

text.p: The Stock Exchange of Thailand on Monday suspended trading in the shares of Bangkok Bank of Commerce Plc.

The exchange had allowed the bank's shares to resume trading in April for a one-month period that ended on Friday. At the time the SET said the bank, which has huge non-performing assets, could see its shares delisted.

State-backed lender the Industrial Finance Corporation of Thailand Plc has since signed an agreement with Bangkok Bank of Commmerce to run the bank. There was no immediate indication as to when share trading might resume.

"Various organisations including the Bank of Thailand and the bank have written to the SET (Stock Exchange of Thailand) asking them not to suspend the shares now that IFCT is running the bank," said a spokesman for Bangkok Bank of Commerce.
"I think the SET might say that they have not received a rehabilitation plan from the new management yet, so a new plan may have to be handed to them," he said.
"Once we have submitted a plan it will then be up to the SET to decide when the shares can be traded again but at the moment no one can really say when that will be," he said.
Bangkok Bank of Commerce was taken over by the government last May after it was found to be saddled with billions of baht in non-performing loans. The bank's shares were suspended then at 16 baht.

The central bank has since stepped in to stabilise the bank's financial situation and has agreed to absorb a large amount of its non-performing assets before allowing IFCT to assume managerial control.
The SET allowed trading in the bank's shares to resume on April 17 for one month in accordance with rules governing suspended stocks of financially troubled companies.

The stock had been heavily traded during the month, falling initially to 3.8 baht and then rising to its daily limit of 10 percent for several consecutive days before peaking at 9.70. The stock closed on Friday at 5.30 baht each.
